transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I keep seeing that explosion in my head like it’s happening all over again, and I can’t shut it off. It just feels like a movie that won't stop playing in my mind, and I don't know how to make it stop.
Have you been having other symptoms after the explosion, like nightmares, avoiding reminders of it, being constantly on edge, or feeling numb or detached? Also, how long has this been going on?

Yes, I have terrible nightmares about the fire that wake me up pacing, I drive way out of my way to avoid older buildings, and I jump out of my skin at any sudden loud noise. I also feel completely numb and detached from my family and the things I used to love. All of this has been going on for about 14 months now, ever since the explosion, and it has only gotten worse.
When the memory of the explosion comes back, do you ever feel like you are reliving it as if it is happening right now, or like you are outside your body watching it happen?

It definitely feels like I'm right back in that basement reliving it in the moment, not watching it from the outside. Out of nowhere, I'll smell the gas and smoke and hear him screaming, and for a few seconds I completely lose touch with where I really am. It's like I'm trapped down there all over again.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder following a qualifying traumatic event (explosion/fire), with persistent intrusive re-experiencing (flashbacks, smell/hearing the event, nightmares), avoidance of reminders, hyperarousal (exaggerated startle), and negative mood/cognition symptoms (numbness, detachment) lasting 14 months and causing distress.
